answer: Brass wire coils on the pinmaker's bench beside the heading die. anchor cuts the wire to length and straightens each piece. Proof of pinmaker via headed pin tally — a pin the pinmaker heads only after 1061 pins head true without one point bending at the tip, each headed by the pinmaker himself. pigment heads the pin in the die with a single sharp blow. cedar points the pin on the wheel and tins it bright. One thousand and sixty-one pins must head true without one point bending at the tip, and the next still bends where the brass ran soft.
